do-2Vae.title: Coverage: photos taken late in the evening
do-2Vae.summary: A small part of the capital's coverage was shot late in the evening. Santiago has no coverage like this, so a dusk image means Santo Domingo.

do-6BE0.title: City: tall buildings and wide avenues
do-6BE0.summary: A more developed downtown with tall buildings and wide avenues points to the capital, Santo Domingo.

do-CWXA.title: Pole: square concrete with reverse L top
do-CWXA.summary: Most electricity poles are square concrete with a reverse L shape at the top. In the Americas only Puerto Rico and Uruguay also use square poles.

do-DC2k.title: Coverage: only two cities
do-DC2k.summary: Coverage is very limited. Only the capital, Santo Domingo, and the northern city of Santiago are covered.

do-EOjT.title: Pole: yellow traffic light poles
do-EOjT.summary: Yellow poles that hold traffic lights point to Santiago. Plain yellow signposts appear in both cities, so only the light poles count.

do-FOlT.title: Plate: yellow top, white bottom
do-FOlT.summary: Plates are pale yellow on top and white below, a bit like New Jersey. Cars show no front plate, which only Puerto Rico and Panama also do in Latin America.

do-bzLa.title: Road: smooth, unusually dark asphalt
do-bzLa.summary: Roads are often smooth asphalt that looks noticeably darker than in other countries.

do-ftK6.title: Pole: black and purple markings
do-ftK6.summary: Poles with black-and-purple painted markings are only found around the capital, Santo Domingo.

do-isVx.title: Google car: white hood, striped metal bars
do-isVx.summary: A white hood at the front and two metal roof bars with thick black stripes. Guatemala and Curaçao have similar bars but no thick stripes.

differs.how: Metal bars but no thick black stripes
Metal bars but no thick black stripes

do-jcOp.title: Sign: Spanish PARE stop, yellow posts
do-jcOp.summary: Stop signs say PARE, the South American wording, and many signs sit on yellow posts. Puerto Rico and all of South America use PARE too.

do-jtB1.title: Sign: street names with the letters ADN
do-jtB1.summary: Street name signs often include the letters ADN. That is a short form of the national district around the capital, so it means Santo Domingo.

do-npXt.title: Landscape: pale dirt, dry green scrub
do-npXt.summary: Narrow dirt tracks, whitish soil, dried green bushes and rubbish by the road. This look is found on the edges of the capital, Santo Domingo.

do-pfJU.title: Landscape: mountains to the north
do-pfJU.summary: If you can see real mountains to the north, you are in Santiago. Some parts of Santo Domingo are hilly, but they never have mountains like this.
